sources.title: Noise management
sources.verified_claim: DEFRA's noise collection links strategic noise mapping, action plans and planning guidance and states noise should be considered for noise-generating and noise-sensitive development.

sources.title: Strategic noise mapping (2022)
sources.verified_claim: Round 4 strategic noise mapping provides estimated road and rail noise across England based on 2021 conditions and supports local action and planning assessment.

sources.title: Explaining the 2022 noise maps
sources.verified_claim: The technical explanation describes the GIS datasets and environmental-noise context; map values are modelled screening data rather than a substitute for site acoustic assessment.

sources.title: Road Noise - All Metrics - England Round 4
sources.verified_claim: Round 4 road-noise data supplies Lden, LAeq16h, Lday, Levening and Lnight-style modelled metrics for spatial screening.

sources.title: Rail Noise - All Metrics - England Round 4
sources.verified_claim: Round 4 rail-noise data provides multiple modelled noise metrics across England; exact candidate exposure requires coordinate/grid intersection.

sources.title: Noise
sources.publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government
sources.verified_claim: Planning practice guidance sets the framework for considering noise effects, existing sources and appropriate mitigation in development decisions.

sources.title: London Plan Chapter 3 Design - Policy D14 Noise
sources.verified_claim: London Plan Policy D14 requires development to avoid significant adverse noise effects and prefer layout, distance, screening and design measures over sole reliance on insulation.

sources.title: Local transport plans
sources.verified_claim: Current local-transport-plan guidance says authorities should integrate transport-noise considerations and notes updated noise action plans are expected for consultation in 2026.
